issues.t: S tronic (DSG) gearbox jerks, slips or goes into limp mode
issues.sym: Jerky or clunky shifts at low speed, a shudder pulling away, the gear letters on the dash flashing, or the car suddenly holding one gear with reduced power.
issues.why: The dual-clutch automatic relies on an electro-hydraulic control unit (mechatronic) and wet clutches. Wear, skipped fluid changes and failures inside the control unit cause rough engagement and fault codes.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read by an Audi or VW specialist. Ask whether the fluid and filter were changed on schedule (about every 40,000 miles). A software update or fluid service sometimes helps; a failed mechatronic unit or clutch pack must be replaced.

issues.t: Cam follower wear damages the high-pressure fuel pump
issues.sym: Hesitation or stumbling when you accelerate, long cranking before it starts, and a check engine light for low fuel pressure.
issues.why: On the 2006-2008 2.0T FSI engine, a small cup-shaped follower sits between the camshaft and the high-pressure fuel pump. It wears through, and once it does the cam lobe and pump get damaged.
issues.next: If you own one of these, have the follower checked or replaced every 20,000-30,000 miles. It is a cheap part; waiting until the cam lobe is worn turns it into a camshaft and pump job.

issues.t: Timing chain tensioner failure
issues.sym: A rattle for a few seconds after a cold start, camshaft timing codes with a check engine light, or rough running. If the chain jumps, the engine stops and will not restart.
issues.why: Early versions of the chain-driven 2.0T used a timing chain tensioner that can lose tension, letting the chain stretch or skip a tooth. Long oil-change intervals make it worse.
issues.next: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle. Have a shop check the tensioner and chain stretch. Replacing the tensioner before it fails costs far less than repairing bent valves.

issues.t: Engine burns oil between changes
issues.sym: The low oil warning comes on between services, sometimes as often as every 1,000 miles. You may see blue smoke on start-up or oily spark plugs.
issues.why: Piston rings on several Audi 2.0T and 1.8T turbo engines of this period do not seal well, so oil gets past them and is burned. This led to complaints and a class action lawsuit.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and top it up with the correct spec oil. Ask an Audi dealer for an oil consumption test; if it fails, the fix is new pistons and rings.
issues.eng: 2.0L turbo 4-cylinder (2009-2013, chain drive) / 1.8L turbo 4-cylinder / 2.0L turbo 4-cylinder (2015-2020) / 2.0L turbo 4-cylinder (S3)

issues.t: Water pump and thermostat housing leak coolant
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell, pink or purple crust near the front of the engine, a low coolant warning, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The water pump and thermostat are built into a plastic housing that warps and cracks with heat, so it starts to seep coolant, sometimes as early as 30,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure tested. Keep the coolant topped up with the correct Audi coolant and do not let the engine overheat; replace the pump and thermostat housing as one unit.
issues.eng: 2.0L turbo 4-cylinder (2009-2013, chain drive) / 1.8L turbo 4-cylinder / 2.0L turbo 4-cylinder (2015-2020) / 2.0L turbo 4-cylinder (S3)

issues.t: PCV valve fails, causing whistling and rough idle
issues.sym: A whistle or howl from the engine at idle, a rough or hunting idle, higher oil use, lean-mixture codes and a check engine light.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve on the 2.0T has a rubber diaphragm that tears with age, creating a vacuum leak.
issues.next: Have a shop check for a torn diaphragm; it is a quick part swap. Fixing it early stops extra oil being pulled into the intake.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, misfires and gradually weaker power, often with a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: These engines spray fuel straight into the cylinders, so nothing washes the back of the intake valves. Oil vapor bakes onto them as carbon and restricts air flow.
issues.next: If misfires persist after new coils and plugs, ask a shop to scope the intake valves. Walnut-shell blasting is the standard cleaning.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure causes misfires
issues.sym: The engine shakes, runs rough or loses power, and the check engine light flashes or stays on with a misfire code.
issues.why: The pencil-type ignition coils on these turbo engines fail with heat and age. Oil or coolant leaks can also damage them.
issues.next: Have the misfire code read to find which cylinder. Replace the bad coil and check the spark plugs at the same time.

issues.t: Turbo diverter valve fails and boost drops
issues.sym: The car feels flat under acceleration, boost does not build properly, and you may hear a hiss or get boost codes.
issues.why: The turbo diverter (bypass) valve has a rubber diaphragm that tears over time and leaks boost pressure.
issues.next: Have a shop smoke test the intake and check the diverter valve. Updated metal-piston versions are widely available.

issues.t: Diesel high-pressure fuel pump failure
issues.sym: The engine stalls or loses power suddenly and may not restart. Metal debris from the pump can contaminate the whole fuel system.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump on this TDI engine can wear internally and shed metal particles. NHTSA opened an investigation into these failures on 2009-2010 VW and Audi TDIs.
issues.next: If a TDI stalls and will not restart, have it towed rather than cranking it repeatedly. Use only quality diesel. A failed pump usually means replacing the pump, injectors, lines and tank parts.

issues.t: Diesel emissions defeat device fix (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing obvious while driving. These TDI cars were built with software that cheated emissions tests, so they emit far more pollution on the road than allowed.
issues.why: Volkswagen Group installed a defeat device on its 2.0L TDI engines. A federal settlement offered owners a buyback or an approved emissions fix plus compensation.
issues.next: If you are buying a used A3 TDI, confirm the approved emissions modification was done. Ask an Audi dealer to check the VIN.

issues.t: Diesel injector line can crack and leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A diesel fuel smell, wet spots on the engine, or visible fuel near the injectors.
issues.why: Vibration can crack the fuel line to injector number 2 on the 2.0L TDI, letting fuel leak onto a hot engine.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell diesel in the engine bay and have the car checked. The dealer fits an improved line and dampers for free.

issues.t: Driver air bag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In a crash, the driver air bag inflator can burst and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: These A3s used Takata-type driver air bag inflators that can over-pressurize as the propellant ages. Some cars repaired once need a second replacement.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA recall search now. This is a free and urgent repair.

issues.t: Fuel tank vent valve can leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell around the car, especially after filling the tank, or fuel dripping near the tank.
issues.why: A weak spring in the fuel tank vent valve may not hold the valve shut, so fuel can escape.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Do not park in a closed garage if you smell fuel.

issues.t: DSG can suddenly shift into neutral (recall)
issues.sym: While driving, the car suddenly loses drive as if it were in neutral, and a transmission warning may appear.
issues.why: A wiring fault in the DSG transmission temperature sensor can make the control unit drop into neutral.
issues.next: Pull over safely if it happens. Have an Audi dealer check that the recall software update was done.

issues.t: ABS and stability control unit can fail (recall)
issues.sym: ABS and stability control warning lights, and the anti-lock system may not work during hard braking.
issues.why: The ABS control unit can fail while the ABS or stability control is working, which can affect control of the car.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for this recall. They update the software and replace units that fail the test.

issues.t: Side curtain air bag may not inflate (recall)
issues.sym: The air bag light may come on. In a side crash the curtain air bag may not inflate.
issues.why: The side curtain air bag inflator can leak its gas over time.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer replaces the curtain air bag for free.

issues.t: Transmission warning light with limp mode
issues.sym: A transmission warning on the dash, harsh or missing shifts, and the car going into a reduced-power mode.
issues.why: Owners of 2015 A3s report transmission faults at fairly low mileage, often traced to the dual-clutch gearbox control unit or clutches.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read right away. Ask the dealer about software updates and any warranty or goodwill coverage.

issues.t: Engine shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine dies while you are driving, the dash lights up with warnings, and power steering and brake assist become heavy.
issues.why: Owners of 2015 A3s describe sudden stalls, with causes ranging from fuel delivery to engine faults. There is no single fix.
issues.next: If the engine dies, steer to a safe spot and turn on the hazards. Have the fault codes read and check open fuel system recalls by VIN.

issues.t: Passenger air bag can switch off with someone in the seat (recall)
issues.sym: The PASSENGER AIR BAG OFF light comes on even though an adult is sitting in the front seat.
issues.why: The seat sensor mat that detects a passenger can fail, so the system turns the front passenger air bag off by mistake.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for this recall. Until it is fixed, seat adults in the back if the light says the air bag is off.

issues.t: Fuel tank pump seal can leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, especially after filling up, or a check engine light for the evaporative emissions system.
issues.why: A seal on the suction pump inside the fuel tank can fail, letting fuel get into the vapor system and leak out, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it fixed promptly. Do not ignore a raw fuel smell.

issues.t: Passenger air bag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash, the front passenger air bag may deploy wrongly or its inflator may burst.
issues.why: The passenger air bag inflator on some 2016 A3s can over-pressurize.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get the free repair as soon as you can.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may come on too late (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving. If all four tires lose pressure at the same time, the warning may not come on in time.
issues.why: A software issue in the tire pressure monitoring system.
issues.next: Check tire pressures monthly and have the free software update done.

issues.t: Backup camera image goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera picture does not appear, freezes or goes black when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Software errors and, on some cars, damage to the infotainment unit at shutoff can stop the camera image from showing.
issues.next: Check your VIN; there are several related recalls. Look over your shoulder when reversing until it is fixed.

issues.t: Passenger air bag may be folded wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash, the front passenger air bag may tear and not protect properly.
issues.why: Some front passenger air bags were folded incorrectly at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN and book the free repair.

issues.t: Front seat belt tensioners may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash, the front seat belt tensioner may not hold the belt properly.
issues.why: The retention of the front seat belt tensioner may not be strong enough.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have both front belts replaced for free.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor connection can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger air bag off light may come on with an adult in the seat, or an air bag warning appears.
issues.why: The connector for the passenger occupant detection module can work loose, which can switch off the front passenger air bag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the module for free.

issues.t: Coolant leak on the 2.0L engine
issues.sym: A low coolant warning, a sweet smell after driving, or pink residue around the engine.
issues.why: Audi issued a service bulletin for coolant leaks on the newer 2.0L turbo engine, usually from the water pump or thermostat housing area.
issues.next: Have the cooling system checked under warranty if you are still covered. Use only the coolant Audi specifies when topping up.

issues.t: Will not start because the 12V battery drained
issues.sym: The car is dead or will not switch on after sitting, sometimes after only a few days.
issues.why: Audi released several bulletins for 12V batteries draining on these models, from control modules staying awake to software issues.
issues.next: Jump start it and have the dealer test the battery and check for software updates. Keep it on a battery maintainer if it sits for weeks.

issues.t: 48V mild hybrid battery fault
issues.sym: A drive system or electrical warning, start-stop not working, and fault code P0A7D in the engine computer.
issues.why: The 48-volt mild hybrid battery can go into a low-voltage protection mode and refuse to charge. Audi issued bulletins on this code.
issues.next: Have the dealer diagnose it under warranty. The fix is usually a software update or a replacement 48V battery.

issues.t: Oil leak near the transmission oil cooler
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the car or an oily film around the gearbox.
issues.why: Audi issued a bulletin for oil leaks at the transmission oil cooler on these cars.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and repaired, ideally under warranty. Low gearbox oil can damage the transmission.

issues.t: Gearbox warning with stored fault codes
issues.sym: A gearbox warning on the dash, sometimes with jerky shifts or reduced power.
issues.why: Audi issued bulletins for gearbox warnings with codes stored in the transmission control unit, including clutch over-temperature codes.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the codes and apply any software update. Avoid creeping in traffic with the brake half on, which heats the clutch.
